correctness.rationale: Definition 2.1 of BML requires the modal relation to be a preorder containing the scope preorder. On a total chain, mutual modal reachability is therefore an equivalence relation with convex classes: if \(x<y<z\) and \(x\) is modally equivalent to \(z\), chain inclusion and transitivity force \(y\) into the same class. Distinct classes are totally ordered, so every modal preorder is exactly a contiguous-block partition, and conversely every such partition defines a preorder extending the chain. Choosing cuts in the \(n-1\) gaps gives \(2^{n-1}\). With \(\ell(d)\) the minimum of the modal block of \(d\), one has \(d\sqsubseteq e\) exactly when \(\ell(d)\le e\); intersecting this with the classifier lower bound in the primary semantic clause gives the stated suffix. The bundled finite verifier exhausts all reverse-edge choices through \(n=6\), corroborating but not replacing the general proof.

final_claim: For a BML-structure whose scope preorder is the finite chain \(D_n=\{0<\cdots<n-1\}\), the modal preorder is exactly a partition of the chain into contiguous nonempty blocks ordered from left to right; hence there are \(2^{n-1}\) possibilities, and every bounded modal successor set is a suffix determined by the left endpoint of the current modal block and the classifier bound.
limitations: The statement classifies the modal relation and its bounded-successor sets, not valuations or full BML models.
